name: no-viewbox-px-and-pt
story: A plain three-line lower third drawn on a 1920x1080 CorelDRAW page and exported to SVG with Responsive off, so the file states its size only as width="1920px" height="1080px" with no viewBox, and carries its type sizes in points.
idioms: width="1920px" height="1080px" with NO viewBox anywhere in the file
px on the page geometry but pt on every font-size (Corel's default text unit is points)
a CDATA-wrapped internal <style> of .filN fill classes and .fntN font classes, applied as class="fil2 fnt0"
the layer wrapper id="Layer_x0020_1" with its <metadata id="CorelCorpID_0Corel-Layer"/> sibling
doubled spaces before the x/y attributes of <text>
#FEFEFE rather than #FFFFFF for white, single-space indentation
whyThisMatters: The authoring page promises a file is sized by "a viewBox (or width+height)", so a size fallback that parses width/height with parseFloat-and-hope, or refuses anything without a viewBox, rejects or mis-scales a perfectly ordinary CorelDRAW export - and the pt type sizes in the same file are the second half of the trap, since 42pt is 56px and a fitter that reads the number without the unit budgets the line 25% too small.
